title: Completeness of bounded continuous functions in the supremum metric
statement: Let $I$ be a topological space and $F$ a field [def-weil-field] with a real-valued multiplicative absolute value, complete for $d_F(x,y)=|x-y|$. Let $C_b(I,F)$ be the set of continuous functions $f:I\to F$ with bounded range, meaning that there is a real $M\ge0$ such that $|f(i)-f(j)|\le M$ for all $i,j\in I$. With $d_\infty(f,g)=\sup_{i\in I}|f(i)-g(i)|$, and $d_\infty=0$ when $I$ is empty, $C_b(I,F)$ is a complete metric space. In particular every Cauchy sequence of bounded continuous functions has a bounded continuous limit in this supremum metric.
